transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~43 mins
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Lina Park (CTO, Catalyst), Jamal Reeves (Head of ML), Sofia Martinez (Infra)

Summary (auto): POC will target interactive UI assistant use case. Primary SLOs: TTFT for first token and steady-state per-token latency; aim for p95/p99 targets per use case. Redwood to run benchmarks and share scripts; customer to share workload and baseline.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:06] Lina: Hi I'm Lina Park, CTO at Catalyst Robotics. we've got Jamal and Sofia with me.
[00:10] Jamal: Hey, Jamal Reeves, lead on ML infra.
[00:12] Sofia: Sofia Martinez, infra eng, I'm on networking and deployment.
[00:16] Maya: Great, on our side Ethan will lead the technical part, i'm focusing on POC setup and commercial.
[00:22] Ethan: thanks. quick agenda \u2014 understand your success criteria, get workload sizing, decide SLOs (TTFT vs TPOT), and outline benchmarks + timeline.

[02:01] Lina: to frame \u2014 we have an in-console assistant inside our control-plane used by customers. interactive feel is critical. if the assistant feels sluggish adoption tanks.
[02:15] Maya: understood, latency is the big driver. are you more sensitive to time-to-first-token versus total time to produce full response?
[02:25] Jamal: for the UI, TTFT matters a lot \u2014 users need immediate feedback, ideally < 200ms p95 for first token. then steady output can be a bit slower. we've seen other vendors where initial ack is fast but tokens trickle.
[02:42] Sofia: also need to plan for concurrency \u2014 typical peak is ~40 QPS for the assistant across our tenant base, but bursts to 120 for a few minutes happen.

[04:10] Ethan: good, that's actionable. i'd separate two SLO buckets: interactive UI (TTFT priority) and batch/async workflows (throughput/TPOT priority).
[04:22] Maya: quick defs \u2014 we're going to use TTFT to mean time-to-first-token (when first token is emitted), and TPOT as time-per-output-token or per-token generation cost/latency \u2014 we sometimes say T-P-O-T in calls, bit awkward.
[04:40] Jamal: yeah that's what we meant. clarify measurement too \u2014 p95/p99 across requests, and also per-token across long responses.

[06:05] Ethan: for the POC i'd propose target draft SLOs: interactive UI: TTFT p95 < 250ms, p99 < 600ms. steady-state TPOT p95 < 30ms/token for average token sizes. For higher-end dedicated we can push p95 < 200ms.
[06:25] Lina: are those realistic for ~40 QPS with occasional spikes? what's the hardware assumption?
[06:32] Ethan: good question \u2014 depends on model size and quantization. for a 7B quantized model on A100 or equivalent we typically see TTFT in the 100-300ms range with good KV cache and batching. if you need <200ms p95 under burst, we recommend Dedicated GPUs or reserved slots to avoid noisy neighbors.
[06:55] Sofia: our security team will push for VPC and KMS. can you run POC in our VPC or do we need Private deployments?
[07:06] Maya: Redwood Private supports VPC & customer-managed KMS; for the initial POC we can do a secured hosted with VPC peering or a dedicated cluster depending on compliance. we'll include those options in the runbook.

[09:10] Jamal: measurement details \u2014 we want percentiles across warm cache and cold-starts, batch sizes, and realistic prompt templates. also measure KV cache hit rate and effective throughput.
[09:28] Ethan: agreed. benchmark plan: 1) cold start single shot tests (cache cold), 2) warm steady-state 2-hour run with arrival pattern matching your traffic (Poisson-ish) for 40 QPS baseline and 120 QPS spike window, 3) microbench for per-token TPOT at varying output lengths (10, 30, 100 tokens). we'll capture p50/p95/p99 and histograms.
[10:05] Jamal: what about batching? our product opens many small windows, so batching helps but adds latency.
[10:13] Ethan: Redwood's runtime uses continuous batching that tries to balance latency SLOs and throughput. we'll run tests with batching disabled and with conservative batching config. we'll also record effective batch size distribution.

[12:30] Lina: can you explain how TTFT vs TPOT are measured client-side? we have front-end timings and we'd like a mapping.
[12:38] Ethan: TTFT measured at the API boundary \u2014 time from request received to first token emitted. TPOT is token-emit interval averaged across tokens or per-token p95. for the UI you care about TTFT (first byte) to start spinner removal, and TPOT affects the overall time to render full response. we'll provide instrumentation snippets and a js snippet to capture these metrics in your console.

[14:00] Sofia: sample workload \u2014 we can generate a 100k request set. average prompt length is 120 tokens with avg output 30 tokens. distribution: 60% short (<=20 tokens), 30% medium (21-60), 10% long (>60).
[14:18] Jamal: also include some multimodal calls later but for POC stick to text.

[15:43] Ethan: good, we'll use that distribution. also need current baseline p95/p99 from your existing provider \u2014 even ballpark numbers help.
[15:51] Lina: we can share our metrics dashboard \u2014 i'll ask Jamal to export histograms.

[17:00] Maya: on acceptance criteria \u2014 does team want a pass/fail on SLOs or a graded report?
[17:06] Jamal: pass/fail is fine: we need TTFT p95 < 250ms for interactive flows and TPOT p95 < 30ms for common outputs for the POC to be considered successful. if we narrowly miss we'll look at configuration and dedicated options.

[18:30] Ethan: ok we'll run the first benchmark on shared/dedicated with conservative configs. our measurement plan will explicitly separate warm vs cold and include additional metrics: CPU/GPU util, mem, batch sizes, kv cache hit rate, network latency, and tail latencies per percentile.

[20:12] Sofia: about security \u2014 SOC2 is a must, SSO via SAML, and encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS. also audit logs for inference requests.
[20:25] Maya: Redwood provides SOC2, SSO, audit logs and KMS integrations for Private. we'll attach security docs; for hosted POC we can do dedicated tenancy and KMS integration.

[22:00] Jamal: one tricky point: p99 can be noisy due to GC, kernel stalls, and cold KV misses. do you recommend measuring p99 over a sliding window?
[22:12] Ethan: yes measure p99 over the entire run and also windowed p99 (5-min windows) to identify transient spikes. we'll also capture event traces for any p99 outliers to attribute to batching or kernel issues.

[24:40] Lina: timeline \u2014 we want results before end of April. is that realistic?
[24:46] Maya: yes. proposed timeline: 2026-04-01 Redwood sends runbook + pricing; 2026-04-06 customer shares workload & baseline; 2026-04-13 run benchmarks; 2026-04-16 we share report and next-step recommendation.

[26:05] Jamal: if initial tests fall short, can Redwood offer dedicated trial hardware for a week?
[26:12] Maya: yes, Dedicated trial available; we'll quote it in the runbook as an optional add-on.

[28:00] Ethan: instrumentation \u2014 we will push a test harness (k6 or locust) plus a Redwood script that can reproduce sessions and collect token timing metrics. we recommend running at least one 2-hour sustained test to capture tails.

[30:15] Sofia: what about model variants? smaller model reduces latency but may hurt quality. we need quality guardrails.

[30:24] Ethan: we'll include a simple quality check: a set of eval prompts and human-pass thresholds. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and model variant tradeoffs; we'll run 1-2 variants during the POC.

[32:01] Lina: pricing \u2014 rough numbers now? we need per-token cost and for Dedicated estimate monthly reservation.

[32:10] Maya: i'll include a pricing sheet with token-based hosted cost and dedicated reservation tiers. exact numbers depend on model and qps.

[33:30] Jamal: are there any gotchas on measurement \u2014 e.g., network between our VPC and your cluster?

[33:36] Ethan: network matters. we'll capture network RTT from your infra to the cluster and include baseline network latency in the report. for best results we can colocate in your VPC or run private deployment.

[35:00] Maya: ok recapping next steps \u2014 we will send runbook and pricing; Ethan will deliver the benchmark plan and test harness; Jamal will send sample workload and baseline numbers; schedule week of 4/13 for the run.

[36:10] Lina: sounds good. minor transcription note: when you say TPOT on the recording it sounded like tea-pot a few times, we joked.

[36:20] (laughter)

[38:05] Ethan: last technical note: we'll report p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and TPOT, plus per-token histograms by response length bucket. we'll include logs/traces for p99 events and a breakdown of latency sources (queueing, model execution, tokenization, network).

[40:00] Sofia: any compliance paperwork? we'll need an SCC and DPA for vendor onboarding.

[40:07] Maya: yes we'll attach DPA and SCC references with the runbook.

[41:25] Jamal: ok thanks all.

[41:30] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the runbook and calendar invite.

[41:35] Lina: thanks.

[42:50] End call.
